Hi everyone,

I’ve been working on a pipeline to improve the reliability of LLMs generating Lean 4 proofs, and I wanted to share the open-core release to see if the architecture is useful to anyone here.

It’s a deterministic search engine (written in Python) that wraps a 7B foundation model. Instead of relying purely on the LLM's latent weights, the engine pushes generated tactic trees to the Lean compiler, parses the stdout/stderr, and forces the LLM to patch its own errors. I implemented a dynamic temperature escalation loop and some basic combination-synthesis (e.g., auto-chaining linarith if the model forgets to close the goal).

To test it, I had it autonomously formalize and verify the Ikenmeyer-Panova occurrence obstruction barrier for VP != VNP at n=5. It closed the barriers zero-shot.

The verifiable environments, math, and telemetry are here:
https://github.com/MyceliaCognition/chaos-prover

I’d love any brutal feedback from this community on the combination synthesis approach, or thoughts on why/where this specific search heuristic might fail at scale.

I don't recognize "the Ikenmeyer-Panova occurrence obstruction barrier for VP != VNP at n=5" at all, so there isn't any signal here that anything useful is happening. How about trying something from https://lean-lang.org/eval/problems/, and making a solution submission?

From README.md:

What Is NOT Included

The following components are proprietary and not included in this release:

  • The adaptive search algorithm (strategy rotation, cycle detection, error interpretation)
  • The neural tactic generator model weights and prompt engineering
  • The combination synthesis engine
  • The full pipeline orchestration with MCP integration

:sweat_smile:
